notes:
Account: payments-heavy ecommerce platform; high volume of refund+chargeback tickets during promotional spikes. Primary ask = reliable tool-calling to internal support systems (TicketX and LedgerPay) to create/update tickets, initiate refunds via LedgerPay API, and escalate to fraud ops when heuristics flag.

Key requirements (from calls):
- Latency SLO: sub-250ms for agent-facing actions (ticket create/update), sub-500ms acceptable for refund initiation (async ok)
- Throughput target: 1.5k tps tokenized during promotions (burst to 5k concurrent requests for short windows)
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for dedicated capacity for predictable latency but need tooling to control token spend
- Model preferences: prefer an LLM + deterministic tool-calling layer; open to quantized variants for cost/perf tradeoffs
- Routing/fallback: must auto-failover to a lightweight rule-based summarizer if model fallback engaged; retain last-known-good ticket state in cache to avoid duplicates
- Observability: token-level billing, per-route latency, full audit logs for all tool calls (required for PCI+A11y audit)

Security notes: team emphasized PCI-scope minimization — no full card data stored; want KMS-managed keys and audit trail for refund operations. GRC flagged need for data residency (EU for EU customers) and SAML SSO for all console access.

Stakeholder quotes: "We can't have refunds slip through during Black Friday — need deterministic retries and idempotency guarantees." — Dir. Customer Ops.

POC success metrics: 1) no duplicate refunds across retry storms; 2) end-to-end median agent interaction latency <300ms; 3) clear audit trail for each tool-call with request/response snapshot.
